clue.text: Fight with entrance fees completely waived?

definitions.meaning: a brawl in which everyone joins in
read literally, an event where nobody at all pays to get in

explanation.definitionFit: A general brawl with everyone involved is a melee; read word by word the phrase also describes admission costing nobody anything.

clue.text: Rubbish engineers initially rejected as safety device

indicators.note: the engineers are thrown out from the start of the word for rubbish

parts.note: rubbish means refuse, household waste
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: Waste from the engineers is turned down because of a safety device.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially rejected' removes RE from the front of REFUSE, leaving the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: An electrical fuse melts to break a circuit, protecting wiring from overload, so it is a protective component.

clue.text: Indication of additive in drug that you get woozier after

indicators.note: the word for woozier is placed after the drug

parts.note: E is short for ecstasy, the drug
woozier, more dazed, is more numb

explanation.surface: A warning about a drug that leaves you feeling groggier afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: NUMBER here is read as 'more numb', not as a figure. E numbers are the codes printed on European food labels for permitted additives.
explanation.definitionFit: On food labels in Europe, a code such as E102 identifies a permitted preservative or colouring.

clue.text: March towards the end of this every twelve months

definitions.text: March towards the end of this every twelve months

parts.words: March towards the end of this every twelve months
parts.note: March is not a walk but the month: the UK tax and accounting period runs April to the start of April, so March falls near its close each year

explanation.walkthrough: 'March' wants to be a verb; it is the month. In Britain the tax year ends on 5 April, so March comes at the end of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The British accounting period for tax runs from April to April, so March lies at the end of each such span.

clue.text: Make new sort of recording of school chaplain maybe

definitions.meaning: to produce an improved new master copy of an old recording
a school chaplain might well teach RE, religious education

explanation.definitionFit: Remastering is reissuing audio from an improved master tape; split as RE MASTER it is a teacher of religious education at a school.

clue.text: Form of insect right inside rock

indicators.note: the letter for right goes inside the word for rock

parts.note: lava is molten rock, and the rock it sets into

explanation.surface: A bug's shape found to the right within a stone.
explanation.definitionFit: A grub or caterpillar is the immature stage of an insect before it becomes an adult.

clue.text: Like style of dress in the south of France

definitions.meaning: a dress or skirt reaching to mid-calf
the French name for the southern region of France

explanation.definitionFit: A mid-calf skirt length is a fashion term; Le Midi is the French name for the southern part of the country.

clue.text: One church composer offering a mass unpopular with sailors!

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
CE is the Church of England
Alban Berg was an Austrian composer

explanation.surface: A musical piece from a church composer that sailors dislike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mass' looks like a church service beside 'church' and 'composer'; it is a lump of floating ice.
explanation.definitionFit: A huge floating block of ice is a hazard to ships, the Titanic being the famous victim.

clue.text: It's bad, one girl being without English, not being able to read

parts.note: bad means ill, unwell
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the girl goes round the letter for English

parts.note: Tracy is a girl's name

explanation.surface: It is a shame when a girl lacks English and cannot read.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means 'outside': TRACY wraps E to give TERACY.
explanation.definitionFit: The condition of lacking the ability to understand written words is the opposite of literacy.

clue.text: Refuse to give incentive to knight

parts.note: a spur is an incentive or stimulus
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: Declining to offer a knight any encouragement.
explanation.definitionFit: To reject something with contempt is to rebuff it.

clue.text: Marble's flaw getting golden when covered in tea?

parts.note: to mar is to spoil, and a mar is a blemish or flaw

indicators.note: the gold is placed inside the meal

parts.note: tea as an evening meal
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A marble surface is spoilt and turns golden after tea is spilt over it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tea' means the evening meal, common in northern Britain. 'Marble's' is an adjective in disguise: belonging to or like marble.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes something made of or resembling polished stone such as that of statues.

clue.text: Fling that's no ending? Only a quick romance!

indicators.note: to fling is to toss about, so the following letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: An affair that never ends? Hardly: just a brief romantic encounter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fling' looks like the definition, a brief affair; it is the anagram signal on THATSNOENDING.
explanation.definitionFit: A single sexual encounter with no relationship afterwards is a brief romantic liaison.

clue.text: When credit is given, it's good to get this piece of paper

definitions.text: When credit is given, it's good to get this piece of paper

parts.words: When credit is given, it's good to get this piece of paper
parts.note: credit here is money paid into an account, and the paper is the monthly summary sent by the lender

explanation.walkthrough: 'credit' looks like praise; it is an entry in an account, which shows up on the record you get from your bank.
explanation.definitionFit: A periodic printed summary of deposits and withdrawals is sent to account holders.

clue.text: What you find in Chinese restaurants? Meat is gluey!

definitions.text: What you find in Chinese restaurants?

parts.note: chops are cuts of meat
to be gluey is to stick, so it sticks

explanation.surface: A diner complains about the gluey meat served at Chinese restaurants.
explanation.definitionFit: Pairs of slender utensils are used for eating at Asian eateries.

clue.text: The man wanting new senior women as role models

parts.note: he is the pronoun for the man

indicators.note: new suggests the word senior is made over into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A man looks for fresh older women to look up to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The man' is a pronoun, not a male noun to define; 'new' is the anagram signal working on 'senior'.
explanation.definitionFit: Female figures admired for courage are idols or exemplars.

clue.text: Dilutant in alcoholic drink man knocked back?

parts.note: gin is an alcoholic spirit

indicators.note: the man's name is turned round, as a drink is knocked back

parts.note: Reg is a man's name, short for Reginald

explanation.surface: Something to dilute the drink a man downed in one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' looks like drinking; it reverses REG to GER. Ginger ale or beer is a common mixer.
explanation.definitionFit: A fizzy ginger mixer is added to spirits to weaken them.

clue.text: Act that gets a bog seat smashed up, say?

definitions.text: Act that gets a bog seat smashed up, say?

indicators.note: something smashed is broken up and its letters reassembled in another order

explanation.surface: A vandal wrecks a toilet seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bog' is British slang for a toilet. The whole clue both defines the answer and gives the anagram of A BOG SEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberate destruction or damage to property is wilful wrecking.

clue.text: Choose the French stuff for extra taste on the plate

definitions.text: stuff for extra taste on the plate

parts.note: to pick is to choose
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Picking out French food to add flavour to a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangy preserved relish such as chutney is served with food for flavour.

clue.text: My niche could be a sooty sort of place

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters of the words before might become something else

explanation.surface: Someone muses that their own little nook might be covered in soot.
explanation.definitionFit: The flue above a fireplace is coated in black carbon from smoke.

clue.text: Producer of old newsreels — jerking and woeful

parts.note: Pathé News made cinema newsreels in Britain for much of the twentieth century
a tic is an involuntary jerking movement

explanation.surface: An old newsreel company's footage is jumpy and dismal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pitifully inadequate is miserable or lamentable.

clue.text: Resets a loose tile

indicators.note: loose signals the letters before are set free to fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A handyman re-lays a tile that has come away.
explanation.definitionFit: A small square piece of stone or glass is used in making mosaics.

clue.text: Raciest poster that's got naughty dinosaurs!

indicators.note: naughty suggests the letters misbehave and get out of order

explanation.surface: A very racy poster featuring cheeky dinosaurs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'naughty' looks like it describes the dinosaurs, but it rearranges RACIEST POSTER.
explanation.definitionFit: The horned, frilled herbivores of the Cretaceous are prehistoric reptiles.

clue.text: A quiet boy getting protection at home

parts.note: p is piano, the musical direction for quiet
Ron is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A peaceful lad finds safety at home.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinafore worn in the kitchen guards clothes from spills while cooking.

clue.text: Wed heartless lass

indicators.note: heartless takes away the central letter of the word for wed

parts.note: to wed is to marry

explanation.surface: A cruel girl gets married.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes the middle R of MARRY.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name stands for a girl, an example of a young woman.

clue.text: Plant ashes in these places?

definitions.meaning: repositories for the ashes of the cremated

explanation.definitionFit: It is a flowering pot plant; it is also the plural of cinerarium, a place for cremated remains.

clue.text: Some care naturally is needed in combat zone

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A little natural care is called for in a war zone.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'is needed in', which are link words; the definition is only 'combat zone'.
explanation.definitionFit: A place of fighting or contest, such as a Roman amphitheatre, is a battleground.

clue.text: Bean covered over in mayo sauce

indicators.note: over says the hidden letters are read backwards
covered means the run of letters is held inside the words mayo sauce

explanation.surface: A bean smothered in mayonnaise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covered over' works in two parts: 'covered' hides AYOS in mAYO Sauce, and 'over' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A legume grown for protein and oil, used for tofu and milk substitutes.

clue.text: Tending to stir up trouble in centre with record of events

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Tending to stir up trouble in centre with record of events': IN + DIARY is clear, but nothing gives CEN from 'centre' without a missing half indicator; no source found
annotationWithheld.clue: Tending to stir up trouble in centre with record of events
